title: IDTM Facility Use and Functioning Guide
overview: Operational guide for the Infectious Disease Treatment Module (IDTM) - covering facility description, operating requirements, safety warnings, and site selection guidelines.

sections.title: IDTM Overview
sections.description: General description and specifications of the Infectious Disease Treatment Module facility

images.description: Complete IDTM facility overview showing three interconnected tents

steps.title: General Description
steps.purpose: Understand the basic structure and components of the IDTM facility

images.description: 3D isometric view of complete IDTM facility

content: The IDTM consists of three pneumatic tents interconnected by four vestibules
Main structure uses PVC coated polyester fabric for durability and weather resistance
Operating pressure: 0.30 bar (maintained by electric blower)
Two patient pods provide isolated treatment areas
One staff pod serves as the central operations area
Sun shadowing nets provide UV protection and temperature regulation
Lightweight flooring system provides stable, cleanable surface

steps.title: System Components
steps.purpose: Learn about the individual components that make up the IDTM
content: Sun shadow net - provides UV protection and reduces internal temperature
Pneumatic spacers - maintain proper tent inflation and shape
Vestibule roof support - structural support for connecting passages
Vestibule pneumatic structure - inflatable connecting corridors
Vestibule inner liner - internal surface for vestibules
Main tent insulation liner - thermal insulation layer
Main tent pneumatic structure - primary inflatable framework
Main tent external cover - outer weatherproof layer
Lightweight flooring - modular floor system

steps.title: Climatic Resistance
steps.purpose: Understand the environmental operating limits of the IDTM
content: Operating temperature range: -32°C to +45°C
Storage/transit temperature range: -33°C to +58°C
Maximum wind speed during inflation: 40 km/h
Maximum operational wind speed: 100 km/h steady, 120 km/h gusts (with proper anchoring)
Maximum snow load: 15 kg/m²
Rain resistance: Fully waterproof when properly set up
Terrain: Can be installed on almost all compact, levelled ground surfaces
UV resistance: Protected by sun shadow nets
warnings: Do not inflate or deflate in wind speeds exceeding 40 km/h
Fabric becomes brittle below -32°C - handle with care
Remove snow accumulation regularly to prevent structural damage
All wind protection measures must be implemented when wind speeds reach 40 km/h

steps.title: Dimensions & Specifications
steps.purpose: Know the exact dimensions for site planning and logistics
content: Total footprint: 276 m² (23m x 12m including clearance)
Main tent external width: 4.70m
Main tent external length: 5.70m
Main tent internal width: 4.00m (min clear width with ⌀35cm legs)
Main tent internal length: 5.00m
Eaves height (external): 2.65m | (internal): 2.40m
Ridge height (external): 3.35m | (internal): 3.00m
Single tent footprint: 26.79 m² (external) | 20.00 m² (internal)
Side clearance required: 1.50m minimum
Hard flooring area: 17m x 8m

steps.title: Pod Layouts
steps.purpose: Understand the internal layout of each pod type
content: Patient pods: Include mesh return openings for ventilation
Staff pod: Central location with access to both patient areas
Family porch: External interaction area for patient family communication
Transfer screen: Isolation barrier between infection zones

steps.purpose: Reference table for tent material and component specifications

sections.title: Operating Requirements
sections.description: Personnel, tools, and conditions required for IDTM operation

requirements.title: Personnel
content: Minimum 4 trained workers for installation
Workers should be familiar with pneumatic structures
At least one supervisor with complete system knowledge

requirements.title: Required Tools
content: Power source (generator or mains supply)
Electric inflator/blower
Inflation hose manifold
Hammer for ground anchors
Pressure gauge for monitoring

steps.title: Personnel Requirements
steps.purpose: Ensure adequate trained staff for safe operation
content: Minimum 4 trained personnel required for installation
All workers must be familiar with installation procedures
Designate one person as safety coordinator
Personnel should be trained in emergency deflation procedures
actions: Verify all team members have completed training
Assign specific roles before starting work
Brief team on safety procedures
Ensure communication devices are available

steps.title: Tools and Equipment
steps.purpose: Prepare all necessary tools before starting work
content: Power source: Minimum 2kW generator or mains connection
Electric inflator: Pressure-regulated blower system
Inflation hose manifold: Connects blower to tent valves
Ground anchors and hammer: For securing tent to ground
Pressure gauge: For monitoring internal pressure
actions: Check all equipment is present and functional
Test power source before deployment
Verify inflation system pressure settings
Inspect hoses for damage or leaks

steps.title: Weather Conditions
steps.purpose: Understand safe weather limits for operation
content: Maximum wind speed for inflation: 40 km/h
Minimum temperature for installation: +5°C
No installation during heavy rain or storms
Check weather forecast before starting work
warnings: Do not inflate in wind speeds exceeding 40 km/h
Stop work immediately if conditions deteriorate
Allow extra time for installation in cold conditions
actions: Check current wind speed before starting
Monitor weather throughout installation
Have contingency plan for sudden weather changes

steps.title: Time Requirements
steps.purpose: Plan adequate time for safe installation
content: Individual tent inflation: Approximately 5 minutes
Complete system setup: Approximately 4 hours
Allow additional time for site preparation
Factor in weather delays when planning
actions: Schedule installation with adequate daylight hours
Plan breaks for personnel during extended work
Allow buffer time for unexpected issues

sections.title: Safety Warnings
sections.description: Critical safety information for operating the IDTM facility

steps.title: Wind Load Precautions
steps.purpose: Prevent damage and injury from wind-related incidents
content: Maximum safe wind speed for inflation/deflation: 40 km/h
Maximum operational wind speed: 100 km/h steady, 120 km/h gusts (with full anchoring)
Wind causes significant lateral pressure on tent structure
Unsecured tents can become airborne in high winds
warnings: NEVER inflate or deflate when wind exceeds 40 km/h
Secure ALL anchor points before inflation begins
Monitor wind conditions continuously during operation
Evacuate immediately if wind speed increases rapidly
actions: Check weather forecast and current conditions
Use anemometer to measure wind speed
Install all ground anchors securely
Have deflation plan ready for emergency
Position tent with smallest profile to prevailing wind

steps.title: Snow Load Management
steps.purpose: Prevent structural damage from snow accumulation
content: Snow accumulation adds significant weight to tent roof
Pneumatic structures can collapse under excessive snow load
Wet snow is heavier and more dangerous than dry snow
Regular monitoring required during snowfall events
warnings: Remove snow accumulation regularly - do not let it build up
Maximum snow load capacity: 15 kg/m² - remove before exceeding
Use soft brushes only - avoid sharp tools that may damage fabric
Heating the tent helps reduce snow accumulation on roof
actions: Monitor weather for snowfall predictions
Establish snow removal schedule during winter operations
Clear snow from all roof sections including vestibules
Check pressure levels after snow removal

steps.title: Rain Precautions
steps.purpose: Manage water drainage and prevent flooding
content: IDTM is fully waterproof when properly erected
Water pooling around base can cause seepage
Drainage trenches direct water away from tent
Ground saturation affects anchor holding strength
warnings: Ensure drainage trenches are clear before rain events
Check anchor security after heavy rain
Monitor for water ingress at vestibule connections
actions: Dig perimeter drainage trench in wet conditions
Direct water flow away from tent foundations
Check and clear drainage channels daily during rainy periods
Verify tent seams and connections remain watertight

steps.title: Temperature Effects
steps.purpose: Manage pressure changes due to temperature variations
content: Air pressure inside tent varies with temperature
Daytime heating increases internal pressure
Nighttime cooling decreases internal pressure
Temperature changes can cause condensation
Extreme cold makes fabric brittle and prone to damage
warnings: Fabric becomes brittle below -30°C - handle with extreme care
Do not fold or manipulate fabric in extreme cold
Monitor pressure during significant temperature changes
Expect condensation during rapid temperature drops
actions: Monitor pressure gauge during day/night transitions
Adjust blower settings to maintain optimal pressure
Provide ventilation to reduce condensation
Allow fabric to warm before handling in cold conditions

sections.title: Site Selection Guidelines
sections.description: Requirements for selecting and preparing the installation site

steps.title: Terrain Requirements
steps.purpose: Select appropriate ground conditions for installation
content: Maximum ground slope: 5%
Minimum clear area: 276 m² (23m x 12m)
Ground should be firm and stable
Avoid areas prone to flooding or water accumulation

requirements.title: Ground Conditions
content: Surface should be relatively flat (max 5% slope)
Ground must support anchor loads
No underground utilities in anchor zones
Soil type suitable for ground anchors

actions: Survey site for slope and obstructions
Check for underground utilities before anchoring
Test soil for anchor holding capacity
Mark installation footprint before setup

steps.title: Clearance Requirements
steps.purpose: Ensure adequate space around the installation
content: Minimum 2m clearance from trees and buildings
Clear overhead obstructions (power lines, branches)
Allow access space for emergency vehicles
Consider wind shadow effects from nearby structures
warnings: Falling branches can puncture pneumatic structure
Nearby buildings can create dangerous wind turbulence
Power lines pose electrocution risk during installation
actions: Measure clearance from all nearby objects
Trim overhanging branches before installation
Verify emergency vehicle access routes
Note prevailing wind direction relative to structures

steps.title: Ground Preparation
steps.purpose: Prepare the site surface for safe installation
content: Remove all sharp objects (stones, debris, stumps)
Level ground as much as practically possible
Compact loose soil to prevent settling
Mark anchor positions before installation
actions: Walk entire site checking for hazards
Remove or cover sharp objects
Fill holes and depressions
Rake surface smooth before laying flooring

steps.title: Drainage Planning
steps.purpose: Prevent water problems during wet weather
content: Plan drainage before installation in wet climates
Dig perimeter trench to direct water away
Ensure water flows away from tent, not toward it
Consider seasonal water patterns
actions: Identify natural drainage direction
Dig trench around tent perimeter
Create outflow channel to direct water away
Test drainage system before rainy season
warnings: Standing water weakens ground anchors
Saturated ground may not support structure weight
Water under flooring can cause slip hazards
